alignments.note: Verbless clause whose expressed subject is a substantival demonstrative: rule 68 puts it on rule 53's pronoun side, so *This is* stays together. Giving the copula to the adjectival predicate under rule 53's general clause is the competing reading, but rule 68 names this configuration expressly.
Improper preposition with a complex supplied frame: rules 71 and 95 keep *in the sight of* whole and head it on the lexical noun *sight*, the trailing *of* riding with the frame as at REV.14.10.
Rule 20: the genitive pronoun ἡμῶν occupies the determiner slot with *our*, so the article realizes nothing.

review_notes: θεοῦ and σωτῆρος are split onto their own English words rather than sharing a head (rules 26, 28).
The *the* of *the sight* belongs to the supplied frame, not to τοῦ, which stands before the genitive phrase the possessive has already determined.
